name: Old Town (Palia Poli)
description: The atmospheric core of Nafplio, where Venetian and Ottoman buildings line marble-paved lanes draped in bougainvillea. Cafes, tavernas, boutiques, and Syntagma Square sit steps apart, and the harbour promenade is close, making it the most walkable and characterful place to live.
bestFor: Nomads wanting charm, walkability, cafes, and culture on the doorstep
cons: Busy and noisy in peak season

name: Akronafplia Slopes
tagline: Elevated old quarter with sea views
description: The hillside beneath the ancient Akronafplia citadel, just above the old town, offering quieter lanes, older houses, and sweeping views over the harbour and Bourtzi. It trades some convenience for calm and outlook, while remaining a short walk from the centre.
bestFor: Those wanting views and quiet within walking distance of the centre
pros: Calmer than the busy old town
Still close to everything on foot

name: New Town (Pronoia)
tagline: Practical residential district for longer stays
description: Nafplio's everyday residential quarter east of the old town, where locals live year-round among supermarkets, schools, and neighbourhood tavernas. It is less picturesque but more practical and affordable, with easier parking and a genuine local rhythm away from the tourist bustle.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads on longer stays wanting local, everyday convenience
cons: Short walk or drive to the old town

name: Arvanitia and Karathona Beach Side
tagline: Coastal edge near the town beaches
description: The southern coastal fringe below Akronafplia, leading to Arvanitia's rocky swimming spot and the scenic path towards sandy Karathona beach. It suits those who prize easy sea access and quieter surroundings, with the old town still within a pleasant walk along the shore.
bestFor: Beach lovers wanting sea swims and calm within reach of town
pros: Quick access to swimming and beaches
cons: Quieter and more isolated in winter
Best with a car for Karathona
